findings.highlight: looks up at the statue
findings.evidenceJa: 偶像を見上げる
findings.governingReading: Looks up at the idol
findings.explanation: The English removes the religious and potentially false-object force of “idol.”

findings.highlight: asks the priest cheerfully
findings.evidenceJa: 愉しむように神父へ問い掛ける
findings.governingReading: Questions the priest as though savoring or enjoying it
findings.explanation: The English changes Gilgamesh’s enjoyment of the provocation into generic cheerfulness.

findings.highlight: The man laughs.
findings.evidenceJa: くつくつと青年は笑う。
findings.governingReading: The young man chuckles low in his throat
findings.explanation: The English removes the quiet, needling manner of Gilgamesh’s laughter.

findings.highlight: As if to make fun of the fact that he has no wish.
findings.evidenceJa: 望みはない、と告げた言葉をからかうように
findings.governingReading: As though mocking the priest’s words declaring that he has no wish
findings.explanation: The English turns the object of mockery from Kirei’s statement into the truth of the proposition itself.

findings.highlight: It is a machine to create the desired outcome for one’s own question.
findings.evidenceJa: 自らに生じる疑問に、自らが良しとする答えしか生み出さない願望機だ。
findings.governingReading: It is a wish machine that can produce only answers one personally deems good to questions arising within oneself
findings.explanation: The English collapses both the internal origin of the question and the self-sanctioning limit on the answer.

findings.highlight: A wish is something that is answered.
findings.evidenceJa: 願いとは自身を叶えるもの。
findings.governingReading: A wish is something that fulfills the self
findings.explanation: The English removes Kirei’s definition of wish fulfillment as realization of the person.

findings.highlight: humans will not be saved if a wish grants itself
findings.evidenceJa: 自ら願いを叶えては、人間は救われん
findings.governingReading: A human cannot be saved by personally bringing about the wish
findings.explanation: The English assigns agency to the wish and obscures Kirei’s contrast between self-achievement and salvation.

findings.highlight: To ten years in the past
findings.evidenceJa: もう十年以上も過去となった
findings.governingReading: To an age now more than ten years in the past
findings.explanation: The English shortens the interval to exactly ten years.

findings.highlight: when he still had a wish
findings.evidenceJa: まだ望みとやらを持っていた時代
findings.governingReading: When he still possessed what might be called a wish
findings.explanation: The English removes Kirei’s distancing skepticism toward calling it a wish.

findings.highlight: The boy grew up according to his expectations.
findings.evidenceJa: 子はその祈り通りに成長し
findings.governingReading: The child grew in accordance with that prayer
findings.explanation: The English changes fulfillment of the naming prayer into compliance with the father’s expectations.

findings.highlight: He could not understand the “beauty” of which his father spoke.
findings.evidenceJa: それだけが理解できないと首を傾げながら
findings.governingReading: He grew while tilting his head in puzzlement at the one thing he could not understand
findings.explanation: The English removes the sustained physical gesture of childhood incomprehension.

findings.highlight: He woke up, raised his head
findings.evidenceJa: 目が覚めて体を起こし、顔をあげた時
findings.governingReading: When he woke, sat his body up, and raised his face
findings.explanation: The English omits the middle bodily action in the moment of realization.

findings.highlight: he wondered why it took him so long to realize
findings.evidenceJa: 寧ろどうして今まで気がつかなかったのかと悩むべきだろう
findings.governingReading: Rather, he ought to agonize over why he had failed to notice until now
findings.explanation: The English removes the normative self-reproach and weakens anguish into wondering.

findings.highlight: The things his father considered beautiful… The boy had never considered beautiful.
findings.evidenceJa: 父が美しいとするもの。それを少年は、一度たりとも美しいと感じ得なかった
findings.governingReading: The boy had never once been able to feel that the things his father called beautiful were beautiful
findings.explanation: The English drops the repeated object and leaves the sentence grammatically incomplete.

findings.highlight: He had a common man’s sense of morality, recognizing that it is correct to be good.
findings.evidenceJa: 人並みの良識を持ち、道徳を信じ、善である事が正しいと理解していながら
findings.governingReading: He possessed ordinary good sense, believed in morality, and understood that goodness was right
findings.explanation: The English removes Kirei’s active belief in morality.

findings.highlight: pursued something he did not have from the start.
findings.evidenceJa: 初めからなかった心を求め続けた。
findings.governingReading: Continued seeking the heart he had lacked from the beginning
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the specific missing heart into an unspecified something.

findings.highlight: tried looking within his body for what he could not find in his mind
findings.evidenceJa: 体のどこかに容れるべき個所がある筈だと探した
findings.governingReading: Searched his body for a place that ought to be able to contain the missing heart
findings.explanation: The English removes the imagined bodily receptacle that motivates his self-mutilation.

findings.highlight: For missionaries
findings.evidenceJa: 信徒にとって
findings.governingReading: For the faithful or believers
findings.explanation: The English changes members of the faith into people engaged in missionary work.

findings.highlight: mental pain
findings.evidenceJa: 精神的苦行
findings.governingReading: Spiritual or mental ascetic ordeal
findings.explanation: The English reduces disciplined religious mortification to ordinary psychological pain.

findings.highlight: Unable to reach the epiphany he sought
findings.evidenceJa: 求め続けた心は得られず
findings.governingReading: He failed to obtain the heart he had continued seeking
findings.explanation: The English replaces the absent human emotional capacity with a moment of insight.

findings.highlight: the sense to feel normal happiness
findings.evidenceJa: 人並みの幸福実感
findings.governingReading: The ordinary lived feeling or experience of happiness
findings.explanation: The English makes the deficit sound like an ability to sense rather than the experience itself.

findings.highlight: even when he had such a mind
findings.evidenceJa: そんな思考回路でありながら
findings.governingReading: Despite possessing such thought circuitry
findings.explanation: The English removes the mechanistic circuit image through which Kirei describes his cognition.

findings.highlight: not in accord with the world
findings.evidenceJa: 常識と噛み合っていない
findings.governingReading: Not meshing with common sense, read here as the world
findings.explanation: The English preserves the ruby reading but drops the written “common sense” layer.

findings.highlight: he tried his best to overcome it
findings.evidenceJa: 全霊を懸けて克服しようと努めた
findings.governingReading: He staked his whole soul on the effort to overcome it
findings.explanation: The English weakens a total spiritual commitment into generic effort.

findings.highlight: to become a priest and preach life
findings.evidenceJa: 神父として人生を説く
findings.governingReading: To preach a way of life as a priest
findings.explanation: The English produces unnatural doctrine and loses the sense of teaching how life should be lived.

findings.highlight: He abode by the rules of God, followed the law
findings.evidenceJa: 神の教えを守り、規律に従い
findings.governingReading: He kept God’s teachings and obeyed the discipline
findings.explanation: The English conflates teaching with rules and turns religious discipline into generic law.

findings.highlight: Yesat every crossroads
findings.evidenceJa: そうあらゆる人生の岐路において。
findings.governingReading: Yes—at every crossroads of his life
findings.explanation: A missing space and punctuation visibly corrupt the transition.

findings.highlight: satisfying his urges
findings.evidenceJa: 異常者である自身を肯定する
findings.governingReading: Affirm or, by the ruby, enjoy his abnormal self
findings.explanation: The English replaces self-affirmation and the enjoy-ruby with gratification of urges.

findings.highlight: What was wrong with him to not even have the option of turning from good to evil?
findings.evidenceJa: その“善から悪に変わる”という選択さえ持ち得ない、とはどういう事なのか
findings.governingReading: What does it mean to be incapable even of possessing the choice to turn from good to evil?
findings.explanation: The English converts Kirei’s ontological question into a judgment that something is wrong with him.

findings.highlight: be born a defective being
findings.evidenceJa: 初めから規格外の者として生を受け
findings.governingReading: Be born from the outset as one outside the standard
findings.explanation: The English turns nonconformity to the world’s specification into a settled defect.

findings.highlight: Call of good sense. Acknowledgment of morals. Trial of justice.
findings.evidenceJa: 良識の語り。道徳の解き。正義の裁き。
findings.governingReading: The telling of good sense; the explication of morality; the judgment of justice
findings.explanation: The English mistranslates the parallel acts and weakens the formal rhetorical progression.

findings.highlight: inquired where the crime was.
findings.evidenceJa: その罪の所在を問い続けた。
findings.governingReading: Continued asking where the responsibility or locus of that sin lay
findings.explanation: The English uses malformed spatial wording and changes sin into crime.

findings.highlight: anger towards something unknown.
findings.evidenceJa: 振り下ろしようのない怒りだった。
findings.governingReading: Anger that had nowhere upon which it could be brought down
findings.explanation: The English removes the suspended striking image and invents an unknown target.

findings.highlight: The priestKotomine Kirei
findings.evidenceJa: 神父言峰綺礼は
findings.governingReading: The priest, Kotomine Kirei
findings.explanation: A missing boundary visibly joins title and name.

findings.highlight: hatred towards a person who was the exact opposite of me
findings.evidenceJa: 正反対の男に対する不快感だけだった
findings.governingReading: Only discomfort or displeasure toward the man who was his exact opposite
findings.explanation: The English intensifies Kirei’s stated reaction to Kiritsugu into hatred.

findings.highlight: interested in the end of this Holy Grail War.
findings.evidenceJa: 此度の結末に関心を持っている。
findings.governingReading: Interested in the outcome this time
findings.explanation: The English resolves the broader present outcome specifically as the war’s ending.

findings.highlight: Zouken’s actions behind the scenes.
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐臓硯の暗躍。
findings.governingReading: Matou Zouken’s covert machinations
findings.explanation: The English keeps concealment but weakens deliberate scheming into generic actions.

findings.highlight: never hatched
findings.evidenceJa: 孵ることのなかったモノ
findings.governingReading: The thing that never hatched, with “returned” as its reading
findings.explanation: The English preserves the written hatching image but drops the return-ruby that connects birth to restoration.

findings.highlight: create something from the Holy Grail that can give the answer
findings.evidenceJa: 答えを出せるモノを、聖杯から産み落とす
findings.governingReading: Have the Grail give birth to a being capable of producing an answer
findings.explanation: The English gives Kirei direct creative agency and weakens ritual birth into generic creation.

findings.highlight: That expression is worn by a man with no interest or desire.
findings.evidenceJa: 何事にも無関心なこの男が、よもやそのような貌を作るとは。
findings.governingReading: That this man indifferent to everything could possibly make such a face
findings.explanation: The English states who wears the expression but removes Gilgamesh’s astonishment at its possibility.

findings.highlight: The answer should come soon.
findings.evidenceJa: 答えは近い。
findings.governingReading: The answer is near
findings.explanation: The English changes confident proximity into a prediction qualified by “should.”

findings.highlight: like an angel that fell to the ground
findings.evidenceJa: 地に落ちた織天のように
findings.governingReading: Like a fallen high-ranking angel, a “weaving heaven”
findings.explanation: The English removes the specific written angelic rank or image.

findings.highlight: Looks up at the distant sky
findings.evidenceJa: 高く遠い天を見た。
findings.governingReading: He looked to the high, distant Heaven, read as sky
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the ruby reading and drops the written theological Heaven.
